artists.biography: Death in Vegas are a psychedelic rock and electronic rock band from the United Kingdom, comprising two permanent members: Richard Fearless (Richard Maguire) and Tim Holmes. Influenced by a wide range of musical genres including psychedelic rock, electronica, krautrock, dub and industrial, the band's sound is constantly changing, moving between live rock sounds, electronica and minimal techno. The band was formed in 1994 by Fearless and Steve Hellier and signed to Concrete Records under the name of "Dead Elvis". Objections from the Elvis Presley estate forced them to change their name, and Dead Elvis became the title of their first album instead.

perplexity.description:
Scorpio Rising is the third studio album by British electronica band Death in Vegas, released on 16 September 2002 via Concrete Records. Named after Kenneth Anger's experimental film, the album represents a significant evolution in the band's sound, blending electronic production with neo-psychedelic and trip-hop elements. Recorded at the band's own studio, The Contino Rooms in London during early 2002, the album features string arrangements by L. Subramaniam, recorded at Trinity Wave Station in Chennai, India, adding orchestral depth to its electronic foundation.

The album showcases Death in Vegas' collaborative approach, featuring prominent guest vocalists including Liam Gallagher, Hope Sandoval, Nicola Kuperus, and Paul Weller. Musically, the record incorporates samples and references from classic rock sources—the title track draws its main riff from Status Quo's "Pictures of Matchstick Men," while "23 Lies" samples The Byrds' "Goin' Back." This fusion of contemporary electronic production with classic rock elements creates a distinctive sonic palette that distinguishes Scorpio Rising within the band's catalog.

Commercially, the album achieved moderate chart success, reaching number 19 on the UK Albums Chart and number 22 on the Irish Albums Chart. The album spawned several singles, including "Hands Around My Throat," "Scorpio Rising," and the double A-side "Leather"/"Girls," establishing the record as a notable entry in early 2000s electronic music. With a runtime of approximately 50 minutes, Scorpio Rising solidified Death in Vegas' reputation as innovative producers capable of bridging electronic and rock sensibilities.
